building.name: Nightingale House
building.completed_conflict: The Market & Octavia context statement describes a building of 1882 at this address; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1878.

historic_survey.note: San Francisco City Landmark No. 47, the Nightingale House — a villa on a generous lot among urban rowhouse neighbours.

historic_survey.survey: Early Settlement Era Styles Historic Context Statement (2025)
historic_survey.style: Gothic Revival, with Carpenter Gothic features and Victorian era features
historic_survey.note: The Nightengale House, San Francisco Landmark No. 47 — a Gothic Revival house that, although architect-designed, carries the lacy bargeboards and pointed-arch windows of the earlier Carpenter Gothic buildings, and shows Victorian-era features alongside them.

historical_record.description: Built for the Forty-Niner and property developer John Nightingale, who had acquired the lot on the west side of Buchanan Street between Laussat and Waller, to a design by the architect John Marquis.

unknowns: The city's statement on early settlement era styles dates the house twice and disagrees with itself: its landmark list and illustration caption give 1882, its narrative 1878. The assessor's roll gives 1878.
